literal: Poverty called a sinner, the next birth and this birth without, will come.
translation: The wretch called poverty comes to deprive a person of the joys of both this world and the next.
modern: வறுமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் பாவி, ஒருவனுக்கு இப்பிறப்பின் இன்பமும் மறுபிறப்பின் பயனும் இல்லாமல் செய்துவிடும்.
explanation: The couplet personifies poverty as a wretched sinner (paavi). It states that when poverty comes, it deprives a person of happiness in this current life (immai) and prevents them from doing good deeds that would secure a good life in the next (marumai). The word 'inri' (without) shows how poverty completely strips away the benefits of both states of existence.
